campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council held public hearings on renewing an interim ordinance related to state Senate legislation, and on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permits for two local shops, California Cigar and Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered applying for a One Bay Area Grant (OBAG) for public works projects and approving consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Renewal of interim ordinance implementing state Senate legislation
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Public works director authorized to submit a grant application
Approval of new consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 6, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council is moving forward with an annual special assessment (Engineer's Report and Resolution of Intention) that will lead to a public hearing and a follow-up ordinance vote later this month. The council will also discuss whether Saratoga should consider becoming a charter city and review early estimates on possible new local taxes and how much revenue they could generate.
keyTopics: Preliminary approval of the Engineer's Report for the fiscal year assessment
Public hearing and Resolution of Intention related to the assessment
Scheduling an ordinance for final adoption at the May 20, 2026 meeting
Discussion of charter city status and next steps for staff
Early estimates on potential new local tax options and revenue projections

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 4, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council is set to approve routine meeting minutes and several contract extensions, including tree care services with Brightview, legal services, and library book purchases through Ingram for the upcoming fiscal year. The council will also review the town's monthly financial and investment report.
keyTopics: Approval of June 16 and June 23 council meeting minutes
Fourth amendment to Brightview Tree Care services agreement
Fifth amendment to the town's legal services contract
Authorization to purchase library books and materials from Ingram for fiscal year
Monthly financial and investment report review

san-jose.title: San José City Council — June 23, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council met to consider several items including historic landmark protections for a property on South Sixth Street, a possible ballot measure on ranked choice voting for filling vacant Council or Mayor seats, and business decisions affecting the airport and city power supply. The meeting also included the standard opportunities for public comment on agenda items and other city business.
keyTopics: Historic landmark designation and Mills Act tax contract for 647 South Sixth Street
Proposed November 2026 ballot measure allowing ranked choice voting to fill Mayor or Council vacancies
Award of contract for large format advertising signs at San José Mineta International Airport
Long-term power purchase agreement with Shell Energy North America
Public comment opportunities on agenda items and other city business

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — June 23, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met to discuss the city's budget limits and financial policies for the coming fiscal year, along with several infrastructure projects like the Public Safety Building and Shoreline Golf Links parking lot. The council also recognized community milestones, including the Kiwanis Club's 100th anniversary and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's new judicial appointment, and closed briefly to discuss potential lawsuits against the city.
keyTopics: Closed-session discussion on two potential lawsuits against the city
Proclamations honoring Immigrant Heritage Month, the Kiwanis Club's centennial, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's judicial appointment
Setting the city's legal spending limit (appropriations limit) and updating financial policy rules for FY 2026-27
Adopting the 5-year Urban Water Management and Water Shortage Contingency Plans
Capital projects update: Public Safety Building construction, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving, and South Bay Salt Pond restoration work

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — July 28, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: Sunnyvale's City Council met for a closed session followed by a study session focused on updating the city's policy for artificial turf fields. The council also handled routine business, including approving bill payments, amending a landfill services contract, and authorizing unpaid utility charges to be added to property tax bills.
keyTopics: Study session on updating the Artificial Turf Policy
Closed session
Amendment to landfill services contract with SCS Field Services, Inc.
Placing delinquent utility bill charges onto county property tax rolls for FY2026/27
Routine approval of city bills and claims paid by the City Manager

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — July 21, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met privately with its lawyers to discuss three ongoing lawsuits against the city. No public votes or policy decisions were part of this closed-door legal briefing; it was strictly an update on active litigation.
keyTopics: Lawsuit: Lixin (Leon) Chen, et al. v. City of Cupertino
Lawsuit: Yes in My Backyard, et al. v. City of Cupertino
Lawsuit: Garden Gate Coalition for Mary Avenue Safety v. City of Cupertino
Closed-session legal counsel briefing on existing litigation

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — July 14, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This notice for the Santa Clara City Council meeting mainly explains how residents can participate, either in person or remotely via Zoom or phone, and how to submit written comments ahead of time. No specific agenda items or policy discussions were included in the information provided.
keyTopics: Hybrid meeting format (in-person and remote participation)
Zoom access details and phone call-in number
Submitting written public comments through the eComment system before the meeting
Using the City Council Legistar agenda page to follow along

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — April 7, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council met to consider changes to how federal housing and community development funds are allocated under the city's 2025-2030 Consolidated Plan. Council members also reviewed new project ideas proposed by individual councilmembers and discussed a possible change to the rules for filling a vacant council seat, including shortening the process.
keyTopics: Proposed amendment to the 2025-2030 Consolidated Plan and 2025-2026 funding plan (affects federal housing/community development grants)
New workplan item requests submitted by individual councilmembers for future consideration
Proposed ordinance change to the process for filling a City Council vacancy, including reducing timelines
Routine approval of past meeting minutes and upcoming council meeting calendar
Preview of agenda items planned for the next regular council meeting

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — July 8, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council opened with a brief director's report covering scheduling and committee assignments, then held a public hearing on a proposal to rezone 470 Olive Avenue from single-family residential to medium-density mixed-use. The change would also update the North Ventura area land-use plan so this property matches the mixed-use zoning already approved for the neighboring lot at 2951 El Camino Real.
keyTopics: Rezoning of 470 Olive Avenue from single-family (NV-R1) to medium-density mixed-use (NV-MXM)
Amendment to the North Ventura Coordinated Area Plan land-use designation
Aligning zoning with the adjacent parcel at 2951 El Camino Real
Director's report on upcoming meeting schedule and council assignments
